extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readership and policymakers interested in international monetary/economic policy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing the British government's white-paper description of a proposed International Clearing Union (the 'bancor' plan) — its objects, institutional design, membership rules and operational provisions. Includes related wartime news but the substantive criteria concern the monetary plan's goals and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: International currency with general acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: An instrument of international currency having general acceptability between nations, so that blocked balances and bilateral clearings are unnecessary; an instrument of currency used by each nation in its transactions with other nations, operating through whatever national organ, such as a treasury or a central bank, is most appropriate, private individuals, businesses and banks other than central banks, each continuing to use their own national currency as heretofore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: remove need for bilateral clearings and blocked balances; operable through national authorities while private actors continue using national currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly agreed method for determining exchange values
rubrics_metrics.description: We need an orderly and agreed method of determining the relative exchange values of national units, so that unilateral action and competitive exchange depreciations are prevented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on preventing unilateral devaluations and competitive currency depreciation as disruptive to international commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantum of international currency governed by world commerce and adjustable
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a quantum of international currency, which is neither determined in an unpredictable and irrelevant manner ... nor subject to large variations depending on the gold reserve policies of individual countries; but is governed by the actual current requirements of world commerce, and is also capable of deliberate expansion and contraction to offset deflationary and inflationary tendencies in effective world demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international currency supply (bancor) should be responsive to trade needs and macroeconomic stabilization, not tied mechanically to gold production or single-country gold policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal stabilizing mechanism to enforce equilibrium
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a system possessed of an internal stabilizing mechanism, by which pressure is exercised on any country whose balance of payments with the rest of the world is departing from equilibrium in either direction, so as to prevent movements which must create for its neighbors an equal but opposite want of balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The union should have tools to induce corrective measures in surplus or deficit countries to maintain overall international balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for starting reserves after the war
rubrics_metrics.description: We need an agreed plan for starting off every country after the war with a stock of reserves appropriate to its importance in world commerce, so that without due anxiety it can set its house in order during the transitional period to full peacetime conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial reserve allocations are to be appropriate to trade role and to ease postwar transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central institution of technical, non-political character
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a central institution, of a purely technical and non-political character, to aid and support other international institutions concerned with the planning and regulation of the world's economic life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution should be independent, technical, and coordinated with other international economic bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of reassurance to prudent countries to avoid discriminatory measures
rubrics_metrics.description: We need a means of reassurance to a troubled world, by which any country whose own affairs are conducted with due prudence is relieved of anxiety, for causes which are not of its own making, concerning its ability to meet its international liabilities; and which will, therefore, make unnecessary those methods of restriction and discrimination which countries have adopted hitherto ... as measures of self-protection from disruptive outside forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective to reduce protective restrictions adopted for fear of external shocks by offering reassurance to well-managed countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership: invitation to United Nations, special conditions for ex-enemy states
rubrics_metrics.description: All the United Nations will be invited to become original members of the International Clearing Union. Other states may be invited to join subsequently. If ex-enemy states are invited to join, special conditions may be applied to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusive membership among Allies with possibility of conditional terms for former enemy states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central banks to keep accounts and settle exchange balances in bancor
rubrics_metrics.description: The central banks of all member states (and also of non-members) would keep accounts with the international clearing union through which they would be entitled to settle their exchange balances with one another at their par value as defined in terms of bancor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement infrastructure routed through central bank accounts at the union using bancor as unit of account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial currency values in bancor and restrictions on alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: The member states will agree between themselves the initial values of their own currencies in terms of bancor. A member state may not subsequently alter the value of its currency in terms of bancor without the permission of the governing board except under the conditions stated below; but during the first five years after the inception of the system the governing board shall give special consideration to appeals for an adjustment in the exchange value of a national currency unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange parities set at inception with controlled procedures for subsequent adjustments, especially in the first five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of bancor fixed (but not unalterably) in terms of gold
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of bancor in terms of gold shall be fixed by the Clearing Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bancor has a fixed gold equivalent initially, but earlier text notes 'fixed (but not unalterably)' allowing future adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotas assigned determine responsibility and credit rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member state shall have assigned to it a quota, which shall determine the measure of its responsibility in the management of the union and of its right to enjoy the credit facilities provided by the union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotas function both as governance weight and as limits for access to credit facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotas initially based on average pre-war exports and imports; periodic revision
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial quotas might be fixed by references to the sum of each country's exports and imports on the average of (say) the three pre-war years, and might be (say) 75 per cent of this amount. Subsequently, after the elapse of the transitional period, the quotas should be revised annually in accordance with the running average of each country's actual volume of trade in the three preceding years, rising to a five-year average when figures for five post-war years are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotas primarily tied to trade volume; revision procedure to reflect actual postwar trade patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of payments by bancor transfers; overdraft up to quota
rubrics_metrics.description: Member states shall agree to accept payment of currency balances, due to them from other members, by a transfer of bancor to their credit in the books of the clearing union. They shall be entitled ... to make transfers of bancor to other members which have the effect of overdrawing their own accounts with the union, provided that the maximum debit balances thus created do not exceed their quota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearing via bancor transfers; allowable overdraft ceiling linked to member's quota.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve fund charges on balances exceeding quarter/half quota
rubrics_metrics.description: A member state shall pay to the reserve fund of the clearing union a charge of 1 per cent per annum on the amount of its average balance in Bancor, whether it is a credit or a debit balance, in excess of a quarter of its quota; and a further charge of 1 per cent on its average balance, whether credit or debit, in excess of a half of its quota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial disincentives to prolonged large credit or debit balances to encourage balance maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on increasing debit balance without board permission and limited unilateral devaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: A member state may not increase its debit balance by more than a quarter of its quota within a year without the permission of the governing board. If its debit balance has exceeded a quarter of its quota on the average of at least two years, it shall be entitled to reduce the value of its currency in terms of bancor provided that the reduction shall not exceed 5 per cent without the consent of the governing board; but it shall not be entitled to repeat this procedure unless the board is satisfied that this procedure is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls on buildup of deficits and tightly constrained unilateral currency devaluation (5% cap) subject to board oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral and corrective measures when debit reaches half quota
rubrics_metrics.description: The governing board may require from a member state having a debit balance reaching a half of its quota the deposit of suitable collateral ... As a condition of allowing a member state to increase its debit balance to a figure in excess of a half of its quota, the governing board may require all or any of the following measures: (I) A stated reduction in the value of the member's currency; (II) The control of outward capital transactions if not already in force; and (III) The outright surrender of a suitable proportion of any separate gold or other liquid reserve in reduction of its debit balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalating conditionality: collateralization and mandatory policy or reserve sacrifices to check large deficits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default declaration and restrictions if debit remains excessive
rubrics_metrics.description: If a member state's debit balance has exceeded three-quarters of its quota on the average of at least a year and is excessive ... the governing board may, in addition, be asked ... and, in the event of its failing to reduce its debit balance accordingly within two years, the governing board may declare that it is in default and no longer entitled to draw against its account except with the permission of the governing board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious enforcement step: declaration of default with draw restrictions after specified threshold and time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual obligation to assist in discharge of a member's default
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member state, on joining the system, shall: agree to pay to the clearing union any payments due from it to a country in default toward the discharge of the latter's debit balance and to accept this arrangement in the event of falling into default itself. A member state which resigns from the clearing union without making approved arrangements for the discharge of any debit balance shall also be treated as in default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective backstop/solidarity: members share responsibility to help cover defaults; resignation without settlement is treated as default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures for members with excessive credit balances
rubrics_metrics.description: A member state whose credit balance has exceeded half of its quota on the average of at least a year shall discuss with the governing board ... what measures would be appropriate to restore the equilibrium of its international balances, including: (A) Measures for the expansion of domestic credit and domestic demand; (B) The appreciation of its local currency in terms of bancor, or ... the encouragement of an increase in money rates of earnings; (C) The reduction of tariffs and other discouragements against imports; (D) International development loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surplus countries are encouraged to take expansionary or currency appreciation and liberalization measures, or support development lending to rebalance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit by gold payment to the union; bancor not redeemable for gold on demand
rubrics_metrics.description: A member state shall be entitled to obtain a credit balance in terms of bancor by paying in gold to the clearing union for the credit of its clearing account. But no one is entitled to demand gold from the union against a balance of bancor, since such balance is available only for transfer to another clearing account. The governing board ... shall have the discretion to distribute any gold in the possession of the union between the members possessing credit balances in excess of a specified proportion of their quotas ... in reduction of their amount in excess of that proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union can accept gold for credit but bancor balances are not directly convertible into gold on demand; board may allocate union gold under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary reserves abroad limited by host-country approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The monetary reserves of a member state, viz., the central bank or other bank or treasury deposits in excess of a working balance, shall not be held in another country except with the approval of the monetary authorities of that country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-border reserve placements require consent of host monetary authorities to limit political/exchange complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing board composition and voting proportional to quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: The governing board shall be appointed by the governments of the member states, those with the larger quotas being entitled to appoint a member individually, and those with smaller quotas appointing in convenient political or geographical groups, so that the members would not exceed (say) twelve or fifteen in number. Each representative on the governing board shall have a vote in proportion to the quotas of the state (or states) appointing him, except that on a proposal to increase a particular quota, a representative's voting power shall be measured by the quotas of the member states appointing him, increased by their credit balance ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board membership and voting weighted by quotas; provisions for grouped appointment for smaller states and special voting rules for quota increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent delegates for non-represented members
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member state, which is not individually represented on the governing board, shall be entitled to appoint a permanent delegate to the union to maintain contact with the board and to act as liaison for daily business and for the exchange of information with the executive of the union. Such delegate shall be entitled to be present at the governing board when any matter is under consideration which specially concerns the state he represents, and to take part in the discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures participation/access for members without board seats via permanent delegates with limited speaking/attendance rights when relevant issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to adjust quotas to correct world purchasing power
rubrics_metrics.description: The governing board shall be entitled to reduce the quotas of members, all in the same specified proportion, if it seems necessary to correct in purchasing power. In that event, the provisions of 6 (8) shall be held to apply to the quotas as so reduced, provided that no member shall be required to reduce his actual overdraft at the date of the change, or be entitled by reason of this reduction to alter the value of his currency under 6 (8) (A), except after the expiry of two years. If the governing board subsequently desires to correct a potential deficiency of world purchasing power, it shall be entitled to restore the general level of quotas toward the original level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quota-level adjustments permitted to manage aggregate world purchasing power with protections for members' existing positions and a mechanism to restore quotas later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information disclosure and consultation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The governing board shall be entitled to ask and receive from each member state any relevant statistical or other information, including a full disclosure of gold, external assets and liabilities, both public and private. So far as circumstances permit, it will be desirable that the member states shall consult with the governing board on important matters of policy likely to affect substantially their bancor balances or their financial relations with other members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and consultation are required to enable effective oversight and policy coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive offices, meetings and periodic reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive offices of the union shall be situated in London and New York, with the governing board meeting alternately in London and Washington. The governing board shall make an annual report and shall convene an annual assembly at which every member state shall be entitled to be represented individually and to move proposals. The principles and governing rules of the union shall be the subject of reconsideration after five years' experience, if a majority of the assembly desire it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational and governance logistics: dual executive offices, alternating meetings, annual reporting/assembly, and a five-year review provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and forced withdrawal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Members shall be entitled to withdraw from the union on a year's notice, subject to their making satisfactory arrangements to discharge any debit balance. ... it should be within the power of the governing board to require the withdrawal of a member, subject to the same notice, if the latter is in breach of agreements relating to the clearing union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exit permitted with one-year notice but contingent on settlement of obligations; board may force withdrawal for breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-member central banks allowed accounts but no overdraft or management rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The central banks of non-member states would be allowed to keep credit clearing accounts with the union; and, indeed, it would be advisable for them to do so for the conduct of their trade with member states. But they would have no right to overdrafts and no say in the management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits practical participation by non-members for trade settlement while reserving governance and credit privileges for members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing board discretion on charging/remitting fees to influence global conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The clearing union may, at its discretion, charge a small commission or transfer fee ... The governing board may, at its discretion, remit the charges on credit balances, and increase correspondingly those on debit balances, if in its opinion unduly expansionist conditions are impending in the world economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of fees as policy tool to discourage imbalances or to respond to global expansionary/ contractionary pressures.
